item.title: Guns, mobs, trucks: The new battle for land
item.description:
A disturbing method of settling property disputes is emerging on the streets of Dhaka: gather scores or hundreds of men, transport them to a disputed property, overwhelm those in possession and establish control by force.
In just three days, four properties across the capital were attacked in incidents involving vandalism, looting or alleged attempts to seize possession, from the demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur and a mass incursion into a Mohammadpur property to an armed attack on a residential building in Adabor and the late-night rampage that destroyed content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio at ECB Chattar.
The incidents differed in their details and the competing claims of ownership remain subject to investigation and legal determination.
But a common thread runs through them: property disputes or attempts to establish possession being pursued through organised manpower rather than the courts.
Detective Branch chief and Dhaka Metropolitan Police Additional Commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that numerous cases of possession and counter-possession had emerged in the capital since the political change of August 5, 2024.
In many cases, he said, people who previously lost possession of property are now trying to reclaim it, while both sides claim ownership and produce documents in support of their claims.
But Shafiqul stressed that neither ownership claims nor previous possession gave anyone the right to take property back by force.
“Regardless of who the legal owner is, reclaiming possession requires a court case,” he said. “Lawful possession must be established through a court order with police assistance.”
“Resorting to attacks and gunfire constitutes a criminal offence, and those involved in such acts will not be spared.”
The emerging pattern has alarmed residents and crime experts because of the scale of manpower being mobilised and the apparent ease with which groups can be assembled for such operations.
At least 27 people have been arrested in connection with the four incidents, according to police information compiled by Dhaka Tribune.
The first of the four incidents took place at Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1 early Friday, when more than 200 masked men allegedly entered the premises, held security guards hostage, looted equipment and other valuables and demolished structures with heavy machinery.
The scale of the destruction prompted questions over the police response.
A preliminary police inquiry subsequently found that officers were at the scene as valuables were loaded onto a vehicle but failed to take effective action before it left.
Shah Ali Police Station Officer-in-Charge Jahangir Alam has since been withdrawn.
The following morning, several hundred people descended on a disputed property in Chand Udyan Housing in Mohammadpur.
An office was vandalised, cash and equipment were allegedly looted, and the property was subsequently fenced off with corrugated sheets.
In Adabor, meanwhile, 15 to 20 men, some allegedly carrying machetes and other weapons, attempted to enter an eight-storey residential building in Shyamoli Housing in another dispute over possession.
Then came the attack at ECB Chattar on Saturday night.
Gunshots rang out as a large group stormed the New Gini Properties compound, vandalising structures and looting property.
Brownfish Studio, established there by content creator Salman Muqtadir, was among the facilities devastated in the attack.
The four incidents over three days have sharpened concerns over whether organised manpower is increasingly being used as an instrument in property disputes, particularly when political change alters the balance of influence over contested land.
For residents caught near the violence, arguments over deeds and possession mean little when hundreds of men and weapons arrive in their neighbourhoods.
Farhad Khan, who lives in a seven-storey building on the main road at ECB Chattar, said his family was terrified by the gunfire during Saturday night’s attack.
“We couldn’t sleep out of fear on the night of the incident. The sound of gunfire woke up our young children,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
“The government needs to crack down on these people sternly.”
Fear was also evident in Adabor.
Monir Hossain, nephew of building owner Aminur Rahman, said the property had been seized after August 5 before the owners legally regained possession in March this year.
The family alleges Saturday’s armed attack was another attempt to take control.
“We are living in fear and cannot even step out of the house,” Monir said. “We seek security from the government.”
The attack on Salman Muqtadir’s Brownfish Studio initially drew particular attention because the content creator alleged that extortion was behind the violence.
Police investigations, however, have so far pointed primarily to a dispute over the property on which the studio was located.
Police say Salman was not the intended target.
Investigators say a longstanding dispute existed involving New Gini Properties and owners of adjacent land. Salman had rented space at the property to establish Brownfish Studio.
A case over the attack names retired Major General Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury and 12 others, alongside 150 to 200 unidentified people.
New Gini Properties director Md Saiful Islam Bhuiyan filed the case with Cantonment Police Station.
According to the complaint, the attackers vandalised computers, laptops, furniture and other equipment and allegedly took cash, construction materials and equipment worth several crore taka.
Those figures remain allegations contained in the case statement rather than independently established losses.
There are sharply conflicting accounts over the underlying land dispute.
New Gini representatives allege that the attackers were attempting to seize their property, while people claiming ownership of adjacent land accuse the developer of previously taking control of part of their land through political influence.
Those competing ownership claims cannot be resolved from the available documents and will ultimately require legal determination.
As of Monday afternoon, police had arrested six people over the attack on New Gini Properties and Brownfish Studio.
Among them is Shah Alam Anik, who told investigators he is a joint convener of Muktijoddha Projonmo League.
Police have also arrested Shahriar, identified by investigators as an alleged main planner, along with Md Mamun, Aslam and Munna.
Investigations and operations to arrest other suspects are continuing.
DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed has promised action irrespective of the political or social identities of those involved.
“We will not consider any political party or ideology; we will focus on identifying the perpetrators,” he said.
“Anyone involved in illegal activities, including unlawful land grabbing, will be brought to justice regardless of their political or social standing. No one will escape accountability for crimes; action will be taken even if police personnel are involved.”
The pledge assumes added significance after the preliminary inquiry into the Radda attack found failures by police officers who were present while property was being removed.
Dhaka University faculty member and crime and social issues researcher Dr Tauhidul Haque said the competition to seize property following political change was symptomatic of a deeper failure of the rule of law.
He argued that organised attacks, shootings, vandalism and looting surrounding property disputes would continue unless law enforcement agencies became more effective on the ground.
He also alleged that major organised crimes often involve links between influential political actors and known criminals, and warned that the apparent inability of police to intervene effectively in some incidents sent an alarming signal about law and order.
“The solution to these problems must come from political leaders themselves,” he told Dhaka Tribune, calling for firm action against those using force to take control of property.

item.title: ‘I brought my children here. Then my grandchild’
item.description:
Shammi Haque stood amid the rubble of Radda MCH-FP Centre on Monday with her 20-year-old daughter beside her, looking at a place intertwined with decades of her family’s life.
She had come here for prenatal check-ups when that daughter was still in her womb. Later, she brought her children here for vaccinations. Years passed, and she returned with her grandchild for the same care.
Now, broken doors, exposed iron rods and piles of bricks stood where generations of her family had received treatment.
“When she was in my womb, I used to come here every month for check-ups. I vaccinated my children here. I also brought my grandchild here for vaccination,” Haque said, pointing to her daughter.
Three days after attackers demolished and looted much of the Mirpur-1 health centre, Haque was among the patients and residents returning to Radda -- some carrying memories, others carrying infants in their arms -- as its staff resumed limited healthcare services from two partially cleared rooms amid the ruins.
An EPI vaccination card lies among the debris at the vandalized Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1, Dhaka. Photo: Abir Ahmmed Shupto/Dhaka Tribune
“Will this Radda ever return to what it was before?” she asked.
Despite the extensive damage, the centre continued providing limited healthcare services over the weekend and expanded operations on Monday, with mothers bringing children for vaccination and pregnant women arriving for consultations.
By 2pm, 56 children had received vaccines.
Routine Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) services and measles-rubella vaccinations were being provided, along with HPV and tetanus-diphtheria vaccines for adolescent girls.
On Saturday and Sunday, staff had administered vaccines outside the centre’s main gate. On Monday, they moved back inside after workers cleared two rooms sufficiently to allow limited services to resume.
The resumption came as the fallout from the attack widened. Police have so far arrested 10 people, while Shah Ali Police Station Officer-in-Charge Jahangir Alam has been removed after a preliminary investigation found negligence and failure by police to act during the attack.
Yet a central question remains unanswered: who was ultimately behind an operation in which hundreds of people allegedly descended on the health facility, vandalised and looted it and demolished much of its infrastructure?
Radda authorities have filed a case naming former BNP Dhaka North City unit member Mohammad Hanif Mia and around 250 unidentified people.
Allegations have also surfaced over political links to people associated with the cooperative that put up signboards at the site after the demolition.
BNP lawmaker Ferdousi Ahmed Misty, whose name has been linked to the controversy by local residents and political figures, has denied any involvement.
“We hope to provide the same services as before and serve people properly,” Radda physician Dr Sahanaj Islam told Dhaka Tribune. “We want these buildings to be renovated.”
But conditions remained difficult.
With electricity unavailable, two fans were running on power drawn from a neighbouring building as mothers waited with their children.
Health workers continue vaccination services at the vandalized Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1. Photo: Abir Ahmmed Shupto/Dhaka Tribune
Sayma Akter, who brought her child for a measles-rubella vaccine, said she had long depended on Radda.
“It feels very bad to see the centre in this condition,” she said. “There was no electricity, and my baby was sweating and crying. I hope to see this place restored to how it was very soon.”
Reshma Akter arrived with her 26-day-old baby.
“I always came here,” she said. “Today, I came and saw the destroyed structure of Radda. Those who did this did not do the right thing.”
Not every patient could receive the service they needed.
Kajol came with her one-and-a-half-year-old son Anas but eventually had to take him home without vaccination.
“They have nothing left. Even the refrigerator has been broken and taken away,” she said.
The centre was attacked around midnight on September 25, when more than 200 people allegedly entered the premises armed with hammers, sticks and locally made weapons.
According to the case filed by Radda Executive Director Dr Nasrin Akhter, the attackers restrained security guards before using an excavator to demolish structures and vandalise rooms used for family planning, ultrasonography, vaccination and laboratory services.
Medicines, two ultrasonography machines, a generator, computers, printers, refrigerators, air conditioners and steel cupboards were among the items allegedly taken.
The police inquiry has since established a critical element of the night’s events: officers were present while valuables were being removed but failed to take effective action before a vehicle carrying looted goods left the site.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said preliminary findings established negligence on the part of police. Departmental action is being initiated, while OC Jahangir Alam has been removed from Shah Ali Police Station.
Police have arrested 10 people in the case. All have been sent to jail.
Radda’s case names former Dhaka North BNP member Mohammad Hanif Mia and around 200-250 unidentified people. Hanif has publicly denied involvement.
The police inquiry has identified individuals allegedly involved directly in the attack and looting, but investigators have declined to disclose whether politically affiliated figures have emerged in the investigation.
Security personnel have now been deployed at the front and rear of the centre.
Workers were also clearing debris on Monday as efforts began to restore the facility.
State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque visited Radda on Sunday and said renovation would begin, while the centre’s management said it had been assured that restoration would be undertaken quickly.
Nasrin said staff wanted security so they could work without fear of another attack.
“We want to continue providing services as before,” she said. “We expect the buildings that were demolished to be restored to their previous condition.”
Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman visited the damaged facility on Monday afternoon and announced Tk50 lakh in initial assistance for its reconstruction.
He also alleged that an attack of such scale could not have occurred without backing from people connected to the ruling party and demanded the immediate arrest and punishment of everyone involved.
Members and supporters of the Communist Party of Bangladesh’s Dhaka North City unit also demonstrated outside the centre, demanding justice and its immediate reconstruction.
Amid the political visits, investigations and competing allegations, however, the most immediate struggle was unfolding inside the shattered centre itself.
Mothers were again arriving with children in their arms. Health workers were again administering vaccines. Pregnant women were again seeking advice.
And amid the rubble of a facility that had served her family for generations, Shammi Haque’s demand was much simpler.
“This place has served my family for years,” she said. “I just want to see Radda return to the way it was.”

item.title: Yaser Khan: Govt working to define journalists, ensure rights and welfare
item.description:
The government is working to clearly define journalists, ensure their professional welfare, implement the Wage Board and protect their rights, State Minister for the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Yaser Khan Chowdhury has said.
He said clear definitions of “journalist” and “mass media” are necessary to ensure that genuine journalists receive their rightful rights and benefits, while those who are not journalists cannot access benefits from the Journalist Welfare Trust.
The state minister made the remarks at a consultation meeting on the draft Cyber Security (Amendment) Act, 2026 on Monday. A presentation based on feedback from the previous meeting was also made at the event.
Yaser Khan stressed the need to formulate an acceptable framework through consultations with relevant institutions and journalists’ organisations to ensure journalists’ Wage Board benefits, professional rights and welfare.
He said ensuring that assistance from the Journalist Welfare Trust reaches genuine journalists was equally important.
“This requires clear criteria for determining who qualifies as a journalist and who does not,” he said.
The state minister also proposed developing a clear framework for professional recognition of journalists and sought specific suggestions from journalists’ organisations on whether a system similar to the Bar Council could be introduced.
Information and Broadcasting Ministry Public Relations Officer Imranul Hasan said RTV Head of News Ilias Hossain, Ekushey Television CEO Abdus Salam, Independent Television CEO Mostafa Akmal, Dr Shakhawat Hossain Sayanto, former president of Economic Reporters Forum Sharmin Rinvi, Manabzamin Editor Matiur Rahman Chowdhury, National Press Club President Hasan Hafiz, Prothom Alo Executive Editor Sazzad Sharif, UNB Deputy Editor Masudul Haque, Amar Desh Managing Editor Zahed Chowdhury and The Daily Star Editor Mahfuz Anam, among others, also spoke at the meeting.
Information and Broadcasting Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam and Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed also spoke at the meeting.
Information and Broadcasting Ministry Secretary Mahbuba Farzana, Information and Communication Technology Division Secretary Md Mamunur Rashid Bhuiyan, and relevant officials were also present.

item.title: Dilara Chowdhury: We do not want the home minister, he must resign
item.description:
Allegations of a deteriorating law-and-order situation have prompted calls for Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed’s resignation, with speakers at a human chain in Shahbagh on Monday citing several recent incidents in Dhaka.
Political analyst Professor Dilara Chowdhury, a former chairman of the Department of Government and Politics at Jahangirnagar University, made the call at the programme organized by “Manch 24” over the attack on content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio, the vandalism of Radda Health Centre in Mirpur and alleged failures to maintain law and order.
Amar Bangladesh (AB) Party Secretary General Asaduzzaman Fuaad, “Manch 24” adviser Faizul Haque, Fahim Mashrur, convener of the Referendum Implementation Citizens Forum, and the convener of Manch 24 were also present, along with other leaders.
At the human chain, Dilara Chowdhury said: “We do not want the home minister. He must resign. Because he has failed as home minister.”
Criticizing the current government, she said: “After the 2024 uprising, I thought it was your responsibility to rebuild the fragile state. But you did not do that. Because you rejected the July referendum, and this was your first betrayal of the people.”
Criticizing the home minister over the vandalism of Salman Muqtadir’s studio, she said: “They broke Muqtadir’s studio. When Muqtadir talked about extortion, he was challenged over a land dispute. If there was a land dispute, there are courts. Who are you to come and break it? And you, the home minister, entered into a war of words with him.”
Addressing the home minister, she said: “Since the day you came to power, you have been a constitutional expert. You want to make a constitution that is not the dream of July. Your job is not to fix the constitution; your job is to fix law and order in the country. You cannot do your job. Leave, resign.”
Amar Bangladesh (AB) Party Secretary General Barrister Asaduzzaman Fuaad said that during the interim government, whenever a national problem emerged, people were told to hold the election and everything would be solved.
He said issues ranging from drying rivers and canals, traffic congestion and rising prices of goods to killings along the border were presented as matters that would be resolved once an elected government came to power.
“But we are seeing that everything remains the same as before,” he said.
Speaking about the recent attack on Radda Health Centre in Mirpur, he said: “The way Israeli forces demolish hospitals in Gaza and the way India’s Hindu nationalist BJP demolishes mosques and temples, exactly the same way, under cover of night, 200-250 terrorists bulldozed a 50-year-old hospital. This has happened for the first time in 56 years. This is the picture of the fertile and prosperous Bengal of the elected government.”
He also condemned the vandalism of Salman Muqtadir’s studio and the shooting incident.
Fuaad called on the prime minister and the home minister to immediately improve the law-and-order situation and restore a sense of peace and security among the public.
“Manch 24” adviser Faizul Haque said the government had been in power for only 6-7 months but had already failed to ensure public safety and protect public healthcare facilities.
He said: “Since independence, I have not heard of any hospital or clinic disappearing overnight. During the fascists’ time, I heard that people were disappeared and taken inside Aynaghar. And during the current BNP government, in the time of Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, we are hearing that 200-250 terrorists have, under cover of darkness, permanently made a public service institution disappear.”
He said: “Those whom you drove away are lying in wait. At any moment they will conspire to undermine your freedom and sovereignty, which we do not want to allow. BNP or this government is not our enemy. We want to tell this government that since you have come to power riding on the blood of 2024, at least run the country properly for 5 years. And if you cannot, step down and arrange another fair election.”

item.title: JS body recommends authentic lists of martyred, freedom fighters
item.description:
The parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs on Monday recommended that the ministry prepare authentic lists of the martyred freedom fighters and the freedom fighters.
It also recommended taking necessary measures to arrange treatment abroad, on a priority and phased basis, for injured July warriors.
The parliamentary standing committee on the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs made the recommendations at its second meeting, chaired by committee chairman Md Manirul Haque Chowdhury at the National Parliamant, according to a press release issued by the National Parliament Secretariat.
The committee confirmed the minutes of its previous meeting.
The meeting also held detailed discussions on important activities undertaken by the ministry over the past six months and progress in their implementation.
The committee recommended that the ministry prepare authentic lists of those who were martyred in the Liberation War and genuine freedom fighters and prepare reports on them.
It also recommended taking necessary measures to ensure that genuine freedom fighters receive necessary benefits and facilities on a priority basis through the Muktijoddha Kalyan Trust.
The committee advised taking necessary steps to keep the Muktijoddha Sangsad functional so that it can play an active role in national politics.
It advised taking appropriate measures to present the accurate history of the Liberation War and remain attentive to ensuring that freedom fighters and July warriors receive the respect they deserve.
Members of the committee and Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ahmed Aazam Khan, State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain, Md Abdul Hannan MP and Rokeya Begum MP, attended the meeting.
The secretary of the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, senior officials of the Directorate of July Mass Uprising, the concerned ministry and the National Parliament Secretariat were also present.

item.title: President calls for unified efforts to build country based on equal rights, communal harmony
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Monday called for united efforts to ensure the rights and dignity of people from all religious and ethnic communities and build a Bangladesh based on equal rights and communal harmony.
He made the call when a delegation of the Bangladesh Hindu-Buddhist-Christian Welfare Front paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban in the afternoon.
During the meeting, the president said people of all communities enjoy equal rights in Bangladesh, where Hindus, Buddhists, Christians, Muslims and people of other faiths and communities have been living together.
“Everyone’s equal rights, dignity and opportunities must be ensured to build a harmonious Bangladesh,” he said.
The president said all concerned must work together to overcome the crises created by the previous government and put the country on the right track.
He said he was aware of the problems, sufferings and expectations of ethnic minorities as well as Hindu, Buddhist and Christian communities.
The president gratefully recalled the important participation and cooperation of the Hindu, Buddhist and Christian communities in making the 13th parliamentary election a success.
Referring to the nomination of more candidates from the Hindu, Buddhist and Christian communities for reserved women’s seats, he said the government was firmly committed to ensuring equal participation of people from all communities in the country’s development and progress.
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir called for forming a national committee comprising representatives of the Hindu, Buddhist and Christian communities.
He said such a committee could play an effective role in coordinating with the government and properly presenting various issues concerning the communities.
“Everyone’s representation and participation must be ensured in the country’s development. No single group can move forward alone,” he said.
During the meeting, the delegation invited the president to visit the Durga Puja celebrations at Dhakeshwari Temple and Ramna Kali Temple in Dhaka.
The president accepted the invitation and assured them of his presence at the celebrations.
The delegation also placed various demands before the president. In response, he stressed the need for collective efforts to help those who had been deprived in the past and assured the delegation that the issues raised by them would be considered with due importance.
The delegation included Sh Ching Prue Jerry, minister for Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs; Bijon Kanti Sarker, special assistant to the prime minister and chairman of the Hindu-Buddhist-Christian Welfare Foundation; Tapan Chandra Majumder, adviser to the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust; Advocate John Gomes, religious affairs assistant secretary and member of the BNP National Executive Committee; Sushil Chandra Barua, member of the BNP National Executive Committee and adviser to the Hindu-Buddhist-Christian Welfare Front; and representatives of the Hindu, Buddhist and Christian communities.
The president’s military secretary, secretary and press secretary were also present.

item.title: Jamaat announces Tk 50 lakh donation for Radda Health Centre
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has announced a Tk 50 lakh donation for the re-establishment of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur, which was damaged in an attack and vandalism by a group of 200-250 people on Thursday midnight.
Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer and Leader of the Opposition in Parliament Dr Shafiqur Rahman made the announcement, while visiting the damaged health center in the city’s Mirpur-1 area on Monday afternoon.
About the donation, he said the party’s assistance would continue to the health services in the area. “This is the beginning, not the end,” he said.
Dr Shafiqur Rahman further assistance would be provided, if necessary, to ensure healthcare services for people in the area.
“If anything, more needs to be done for the treatment of the people of this area, we will do it, Insha’Allah,” he said.
Expressing concern over the attack, vandalism and looting at the health center, the Jamaat chief said, “Surely, no one would have dared to commit such a serious crime without the shelter and patronage of the ruling party.”
He said whoever was involved in the incident should be brought to the law.
The leader of the opposition also expressed concern over the deterioration of the country’s law and order situation, saying that the government must take immediate steps so that no miscreant can commit any antisocial or criminal activities anywhere in the country.
He alleged that “mob violence is taking place across the country under the shelter and patronage of the ruling party.”
He called for legal action against those involved in the Radda incident and urged the authorities to take steps to reopen the health center.

item.title: Now crude bomb-like objects found at Buddhijibi Graveyard
item.description:
The Special Response Battalion (SRB) has found several objects resembling crude bombs at the Shaheed Buddhijibi Graveyard in the capital.
The SRB Bomb Disposal Unit is working to neutralise the objects.
The information was disclosed in a message sent by the SRB on Monday night.
According to the message, a special team from SRB-2’s Special Company has cordoned off the site where the bomb-like objects were found and placed it under a security perimeter.
The SRB Bomb Disposal Unit is carrying out operations at the scene.
Earlier in the day, around 20 crude bombs and petrol bomb-like objects were recovered from the former International Trade Fair ground in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar.
Monirul Islam, officer-in-charge of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station, said: “SRB found some bomb-like objects abandoned at the fairground. They are working to defuse them.”
Meanwhile, law enforcement personnel cordoned off the area and restricted public movement for security reasons.

item.title: 20 crude, petrol bombs recovered from former trade fair ground
item.description: Twenty crude bombs and petrol bombs have been recovered from the former Trade Fair ground beside the Bangladesh China Friendship Conference Center in the capital. Additional DIG Naimul Hasan, commander of SRB-2, confirmed the matter. Earlier on Monday evening, members of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) recovered the explosives. The SRB said, that on Monday evening, 20 unexploded crude bombs and petrol bombs were recovered from the former Trade Fair ground. The law enforcement authorities also said that necessary measures were being taken to neutralize the recovered explosives. Naimul Hasan said, that the explosives were recovered during an operation at the former Trade Fair ground based on confidential information. A bomb disposal unit was called in to neutralize the explosives, and the team was working at the scene. It was not immediately known how the explosives came to be there or who was involved. SRB Squadron Leader Nifaz Rahman said, “Our team reached the scene and began working. Several bombs were found inside a bag. The bomb disposal unit has already arrived and neutralized some of them. There are some more, which will be taken outside the public area and neutralized later. Approximately 20 crude bombs and petrol bombs were found here.” Law enforcement personnel at the scene have cordoned off the entire area. Movement of members of the public is also being restricted for security reasons.

item.title: DSCC launches 12-day Aedes larvae survey to curb dengue
item.description:
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) on Monday launched a 12-day monsoon survey of Aedes mosquito larvae to identify breeding grounds and dengue-prone areas and strengthen data-driven mosquito control efforts.
DSCC Administrator and Liberation War veteran Md Abdus Salam formally inaugurated the survey at Nagar Bhaban on Monday. The survey began on September 27 and will continue until October 8. Under the initiative, 30 randomly selected households in each of the DSCC’s 75 wards, 2,250 households in total, are being surveyed using scientific methods.
The survey aims to identify mosquito hotspots and major breeding sources across the city corporation’s 10 zones.
A total of 72 field workers from the DSCC and the Directorate General of Health Services’ Communicable Disease Control unit are taking part in the survey. The KoboToolbox application is being used to ensure accurate and transparent data collection.
The collected data will be analysed to determine the Breteau Index (BI), House Index (HI), Container Index (CI) and Pupa Index (PI). Based on the Breteau Index, areas will be classified as high risk (BI 20 or above), moderate risk (BI 10–19), or low risk (BI below 10).
The DSCC will then intensify mosquito-control measures in identified hotspots, including cleaning drives, larvicide application and special crash programmes.
Speaking at the inauguration, Abdus Salam said scientific identification of Aedes breeding grounds and high-risk areas was essential for effective dengue control.
“This survey will provide an accurate picture of the current situation in DSCC areas, based on which we will take effective measures,” he said.
He also urged residents to help prevent Aedes breeding by keeping rooftops, balconies, construction sites and surrounding areas free of stagnant water.
“Aedes mosquitoes can be controlled only when citizens join hands with the city corporation,” he added.
Earlier, a pre-monsoon survey found larval density above the prescribed threshold in 63 of the DSCC’s 75 wards, while 27 wards were classified as highly vulnerable. Based on those findings, the city corporation conducted crash programmes in the affected areas.

item.title: Nahid demands home minister’s removal
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam on Monday said restoring law and order in the country would not be possible as long as Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed remains in office as he has “failed to fulfill his responsibilities”.
“We believe he has already failed. If a person has failed, he cannot and should not remain in charge,” Nahid said at a press briefing following a meeting at the party office in the capital.
He said the home minister should step down to set an example of accountability within the government.
“We have already seen a few reshuffles in the cabinet. So, now he should be removed. An example needs to be set that if someone fails in their duties, they must step down and make way for a successor,” he said.
“This will send a message to everyone including the government officials working under him,” he added.
Nahid accused the government of failing to rein in its party activists.
Referring to the recent demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur and the attack on content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio, he said the incidents reflected the deteriorating law and order situation.
He alleged that law enforcement agencies remained inactive during the attacks, raising questions about the government's ability to ensure public safety.
“The government had promised that the law-and-order situation would improve after an elected government came to power. But the situation has deteriorated further,” he said.
The NCP leader also accused the government of politicizing public recruitment, citing the exclusion of candidates from the primary school teacher recruitment process following police verification.
He said qualified candidates should not be disqualified without specific evidence of their involvement in criminal or anti-state activities.
Nahid said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's recent address to the United Nations General Assembly had failed to reflect the expectations and concerns of Bangladeshi people.
He said the prime minister missed an opportunity to highlight key national concerns including the ongoing energy crisis, border killings, push-ins from India, the Rohingya crisis and the implementation of the Teesta project.
On constitutional reforms, Nahid rejected the government's initiative to form a parliamentary committee to amend the Constitution, arguing that fundamental reforms could not be achieved through the regular amendment process.
He called for the immediate convening of the Constitution Reform Council to implement the July National Charter, warning that the NCP would continue its programs and move towards tougher action if the government fails to do so.
Nahid also expressed concern over the proposed Cyber Security Act, alleging that it could curtail freedom of expression and be used to suppress criticism of the government.
On the upcoming local government elections, he said the NCP would contest independently and support candidates committed to combating extortion, terrorism and land grabbing.
Senior party leaders Akhter Hossen, Sarjis Alam, Hasnat Abdullah, Nasiruddin Patwari, among others, were also present at the meeting.

item.title: Milon: Finance Ministry working on separate pay scale for MPO-listed teachers
item.description:
The Finance Ministry is working on a separate pay scale for teachers and employees of MPO-listed educational institutions, Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon said on Monday.
He made the remarks while speaking to journalists after a meeting at the Secretariat.
The Finance Ministry published the gazette for the ninth national pay scale for government employees on September 21.
Following this, the Education Ministry said teachers and employees of MPO-listed private schools, colleges, madrasas and technical institutions would also be brought under the new pay scale.
A separate gazette will be issued to include MPO-listed teachers and employees in the pay scale, according to the ministry. The matter has already been discussed at senior levels of the Education and Finance ministries.
The process was delayed as the prime minister and her education adviser Mahdi Amin were out of the country, ministry sources said. It gained momentum after their return.
Asked about the issue at a press conference, Milon said, “The Finance Ministry will issue a separate notification on the pay scale for MPO-listed teachers and employees. They are working on the matter.”
Ministry sources said the Education Ministry must first send a letter to the Finance Ministry seeking approval to include private-sector teachers in the ninth pay scale. The Finance Ministry will then issue a gazette formally approving the benefits for MPO-listed staff.
A separate gazette cannot be issued without the Finance Ministry’s approval, the sources added.
More than 600,000 teachers and employees nationwide are currently covered by the MPO scheme, according to the Education Ministry. Of them, around 400,000 are under the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education, nearly 200,000 under the Directorate of Madrasa Education, and more than 23,000 under the Directorate of Technical Education.

item.title: IFIC Bank supports DU students with research grants, scholarships
item.description:
IFIC Bank has awarded research grants and scholarships to students of the University of Dhaka as part of its initiative to promote academic research and support meritorious students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds.
The awards were presented at the “IFIC Bank Trust Fund Research Grant and Scholarship Award Ceremony 2026,” held on Monday, September 28, at the Conference Hall of Nabab Nawab Ali Chowdhury Senate Bhaban, University of Dhaka.
The program was chaired by Prof M Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, treasurer of the University of Dhaka and chairman of the IFIC Bank Trust Fund.
Among those present were Md Monitur Rahman, deputy managing director and chief information officer of IFIC Bank; Helal Ahmed, chief of branch business; Mohammad Shahin Uddin, head of treasury; Prof Saifuddin Md Tareeq, Dean of the Faculty of Engineering and Technology, University of Dhaka; and Prof Al Amin, Dean of the Faculty of Business Studies.
Senior officials from both institutions, along with faculty members, students and guardians, also attended the event.
Munsi Shams Uddin Ahmed, acting registrar of the University of Dhaka, conducted the program.
During the ceremony, research grants were awarded to 50 students and scholarships were awarded to 30 students from the 2022–23 and 2023–24 academic sessions.
Established in 2012, the IFIC Bank Trust Fund supports students of the University of Dhaka through research grants and scholarships.
To date, more than 450 students from different faculties have benefited from the initiative.

item.title: NBR to return to monthly VAT return process
item.description:
The quarterly VAT return system was introduced to simplify business operations and reduce the accounting burden on small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
However, within just a few months of its implementation, the government is deciding to make a major reversal in this VAT payment rule.
Although the budget for the current FY27 provided for submitting VAT returns and making payments every three months, it has resulted in a severe collapse in revenue collection in practice.
Due to the new rule, cash is not being deposited into the government treasury on time, directly impacting the government's regular operating expenses.
In the first two months of implementation alone, VAT collection dropped by nearly 20% or Tk crore compared to the same period last fiscal year.
At the same time, the number of institutions submitting returns has also relatively declined.
Amid the country's ongoing situation, the revenue shortfall has created major concerns for the government in meeting necessary social, economic, and energy expenses.
Consequently, to stop public funds from remaining tied up with businesses for long periods and to normalize revenue flow, the National Board of Revenue (NBR) is preparing to swiftly revert to the previous monthly VAT return submission process through an ordinance.
According to NBR data, nearly 38% of total revenue comes from VAT.
In the first two months (July and August) of the current FY27, a total of Tk crore in VAT was collected.
For the current FY27, the NBR's total revenue collection target has been set at Tk crore.
Out of this, Tk crore is to be collected from the VAT sector alone.
Md Ainul Islam, former general secretary of the Bangladesh Economic Association, stated that to make the economy self-reliant in the long run, there is no alternative to increasing the tax-to-GDP ratio. For this, radical changes must be brought to the NBR’s traditional tax collection system.
Rather than imposing new tax burdens on existing taxpayers, the tax net must be expanded significantly.
New emerging sectors of the economy must be brought under the tax net to ensure revenue growth.
To make this entire process successful, it is essential to substantially enhance the institutional and technological capacity of the NBR.

item.title: Govt to raise $1bn in maiden sovereign bond issue
item.description:
Bangladesh is set to issue sovereign bonds in the international market for the first time.
The government aims to raise $500 million to $1 billion by selling these bonds within the next three months.
Following meetings with institutional investors in Europe and New York, Dhaka has received strong signals of interest.
Fifteen major investment firms—including global financial giants BlackRock, Pacific Investment Management Company (PIMCO), TPG Inc., Macquarie, GoldenTree Asset Management, and MetLife—have shown preliminary interest in the bond issuance.
According to a report by US media outlet Bloomberg, a senior government official stated that Bangladesh is preparing to collect $500 million to $1 billion over the next three months through its debut foreign-currency sovereign bond sale.
Speaking to Bloomberg on Saturday, Tanvir Shahriar Ghani, special assistant to the prime minister on investments and capital markets, said JPMorgan Chase & Co. will manage the upcoming bond issue.
However, the plan still requires final approval from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
This debt sale initiative comes as global borrowing costs have risen following recent interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve, forcing developing nations to adapt to higher borrowing expenses.
Ghani, who heads the government's bond issuance committee, noted that this environment is influencing Dhaka's approach regarding pricing.
"The interest rate has increased by 25 basis points, which will affect yields across emerging markets. We intend to be cautious regarding bond pricing and proceed accordingly," Tanvir Shahriar said.
He added that while balancing its financing requirements, the government remains "sensitive" to the cost of capital.
Investor demand for Bangladesh’s inaugural global debt offering appears strong following non-deal roadshows with institutional investors in Europe last week.
"The level of interest in the sovereign bond is extremely high," Tanvir Shahriar remarked. He added that subsequent meetings in New York were strictly focused on institutional investors.
Ghani declined to disclose specific details about the transaction structure, noting that the deal involves certain "legal sensitivities" that must be handled with care.
Bangladesh Bank first introduced the concept of issuing sovereign debt to foreign investors in 2012.
Although the government revisited the idea in later years, it was never implemented until now.

item.title: Dooley pleased with Bangladesh's response despite Singapore defeat
item.description:
Bangladesh head coach Thomas Dooley was pleased with his side's response to their heavy defeat against Malaysia despite suffering a narrow 1-0 loss to Singapore in their second Group A match of the FIFA Asean Cup 2026 in Jakarta on Monday.
Harhys Stewart's 35th-minute header proved decisive at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium, but Bangladesh produced a much-improved performance after their 3-0 defeat to Malaysia in their tournament opener.
“We certainly saw a different team tonight compared to the last match. I am very pleased with the way the players responded,” Dooley said after the match.
Bangladesh created several opportunities in the second half but could not find an equaliser. Shamit Shome headed over the crossbar from a Saad Uddin cross, while Saad headed wide from Fahamedul Islam's delivery.
Dooley felt Bangladesh could have secured a better result had they been more clinical in the closing stages.
“We managed to play good football against Singapore, and had we capitalized on our scoring opportunities in the final 20 minutes, the result might have been even more positive for us,” he said.
“Shamit had a great chance—he missed the header—but the players' effort was excellent.”
The German-American coach said the performance showed Bangladesh can compete against higher-ranked Southeast Asian opposition when they maintain their intensity throughout the match.
“I think everyone has realized that if we fight hard and don't give the opposition too much space, we can compete with them,” Dooley said.
He also pointed to the lack of regular domestic competition as a major gap between Bangladesh and their Southeast Asian opponents.
“The domestic competition we have in Bangladesh isn't very extensive; we don't have leagues like those in Malaysia, Singapore, or Indonesia,” he said.
“Having a league is crucial because it allows players to play matches every week and learn from their mistakes. That is the gap we face.”
Dooley said the Asean Cup has provided valuable preparation ahead of the SAFF Championship, particularly against higher-ranked opposition.
“We need to understand where we stand. We are happy to be playing in this tournament because it features teams like Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore—all of whom are ranked far higher than us,” he said.
“We didn't come here expecting to beat everyone; rather, we came to identify our mistakes and learn from them.”
Dooley identified finishing as Bangladesh's biggest weakness, saying the team lacks a clinical striker.
“Our biggest issue is scoring goals; the team lacks a clinical striker capable of consistently finding the back of the net,” he said.
Comparing Monday's performance with the defeat to Malaysia, Dooley praised his players' commitment.
“We didn't come here for a holiday; we came to compete against higher-ranked teams. You cannot compete with only eight or nine players fighting; everyone has to give 100 percent,” he said.
“Today, from the very first second, everyone fought, closed down spaces, and chased the ball.”
He also welcomed Bangladesh's improved approach in possession, with the team relying less on long balls.
“We didn't just play long balls like in the previous match,” he said. “I want the team to play by maintaining possession.”
Bangladesh will conclude their group-stage campaign against hosts Indonesia at the same venue on Thursday.

item.title: Iran says its UN delegation does not plan further US talks
item.description:
Iran’s delegation in New York for the UN General Assembly is not planning further talks with the United States, state media reported Monday, after US President Donald Trump said he expected more negotiations soon.
Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks mediated by Qatar on the sidelines of the UN meeting, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for ending their war and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
But state news agency IRNA on Monday quoted an unnamed source close to the UN delegation as saying there were no more talks scheduled.
“Iran’s delegation in New York has no plans for negotiations with the United States,” IRNA quoted the source as saying.
“Iran’s views and positions were conveyed clearly and explicitly to the US side... via a Qatari mediator,” IRNA said.
The Iranian delegation would return to Tehran on Tuesday, the news agency added.
Trump on Saturday publicly rejected Iran’s latest proposal for ending the war, but told US media outlet Axios on Sunday that he expected talks to resume in the coming days.
Despite Trump’s rejection, Tehran has said it is waiting for a formal US response before deciding on its next steps.
Axios said further indirect talks mediated by Qatar could take place as early as Monday.
Last week’s discussions were held by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.
The Strait of Hormuz lies at the heart of the conflict, which began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.
The strategic shipping route carried one fifth of the world’s oil and gas before the war began.
But Tehran imposed a blockade on Hormuz after the war started, prompting Washington to respond with its own blockade on Iranian ports.
As a precondition for ending its blockade, Iran is demanding a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah has been battling Israeli forces.
It is also demanding the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade.
Fighting between the two sides has subsided in recent weeks, with the US not striking Iran since September 1, but Tehran has continued to target commercial vessels in Hormuz.

item.title: Myanmar military airstrike kills 33 in market area
item.description:
A military airstrike on a market in western Myanmar killed 33 people on Monday and wounded 36 more, a rebel faction which controls the area said in a statement.
The Arakan Army said the death toll of the strike around midday (0530 GMT) on a market and adjacent bridge in Kyauktaw town of Rakhine state “may continue to increase.”
A witness who requested anonymity for safety reasons saw more than 30 bodies at the scene on Monday afternoon, where human remains were visible among smouldering wreckage and cratered roads.
It was not possible to reach the military for comment.
The western state of Rakhine is witnessing some of the direst conditions in Myanmar’s civil war which was unleashed by a 2021 military coup.

item.title: New Delhi to ban construction for six weeks to tackle air pollution
item.description:
New Delhi will ban construction for six weeks in the country’s capital, as part of a slew of measures announced on Monday to tackle the city’s air pollution.
Delhi, a sprawling megacity of 30 million people, is regularly ranked among the world’s most polluted capitals due to a mix of emissions from power plants, heavy traffic, construction activity and the burning of crop stubble.
The construction ban will run from December 10 to January 20 as part of a winter action plan which will include restrictions on vehicular traffic aimed at encouraging residents to use public transport.
“Early implementation of these stringent measures would help prevent the city’s air from reaching hazardous levels during winter,” Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa told reporters.
Air pollution in Delhi regularly reaches dangerous levels during winter months when cooler air traps pollutants close to the ground.
A study in The Lancet Planetary Health in 2024 estimated that 3.8 million deaths in India between 2009 and 2019 were linked to air pollution.
Levels of cancer-causing PM 2.5 microparticles often hit more than 300 micrograms per cubic meter in the city, 20 times the World Health Organization’s recommended daily maximum.
Government-led initiatives such as partial restrictions on fossil fuel-powered transport and water trucks spraying mist to clear the air have failed to make a noticeable impact.
Under the new plan, Sirsa said “Staggered office timings will be implemented from November 1 to February 28 to reduce peak-hour traffic congestion and vehicular emissions.”
Parking fees will also be doubled from November 1 to discourage the use of private vehicles.
“We hope we will do better than last year and keep on improving the situation from year to year,” Sirsa said.

item.title: Russian drone hits Kyiv’s Academy of Sciences
item.description:
One woman was killed and three people wounded in a Russian drone strike that triggered a fire inside Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences in central Kyiv on Monday, authorities said.
Videos shared on social media showed people leaning out of windows for fresh air as thick black smoke and bright orange flames engulfed part of the historic building.
The site is in the very center of Kyiv -- usually well protected from Russian attacks -- close to the German embassy, a famed cathedral, the national opera and government buildings.
The Ukrainian air force had earlier issued an alert for Kyiv, warning of “drones moving toward the city.”
“One woman was killed. Three people were wounded. Medics have taken them to the hospital,” said Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko.
“A rescue operation is underway: crews are putting out the fire and searching for people who may have been trapped inside,” added Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
A business center in the eastern city of Dnipro was also hit, he said.
“Sadly, people have been killed,” Zelensky said, without giving more details on the casualties.
Moscow has been pounding Kyiv with drone and missile attacks for months, with intensifying strikes bringing the city to a standstill as air raid sirens blast out multiple times a day.
Cultural sites, government buildings and schools have all been targeted in the attacks, Ukraine says.
Earlier this month, a Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security services.
In recent months, Russia has been deploying newer jet-powered drones that move faster and are harder to intercept than the traditional models, based on Iranian Shahed drones.

item.title: PM to honour best teachers on World Teachers’ Day
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will honour and award the country’s best teachers on October 5, marking World Teachers’ Day, Education and Primary and Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon said on Monday.
He made the remarks at a meeting of the National Steering Committee on World Teachers’ Day at the Education Ministry’s conference room.
“The country’s best teachers will be honoured and awarded on World Teachers’ Day. The government is working to enhance teachers’ dignity and status and improve the quality of education,” the minister said.
Milon also said action would be taken against those found negligent in evaluating answer scripts of this year’s Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examinations.
He urged teachers to perform their duties responsibly and maintain quality standards while evaluating exam papers.
Regarding the recruitment of assistant teachers for government primary schools, the minister said misinformation was being spread in the media about the issuance of appointment letters.
“The ministry is working to complete the recruitment process properly,” he said.
He said the issuance of appointment letters was taking some time due to necessary verification and scrutiny, which would continue until October 1.
The minister urged candidates not to be misled by false or confusing information about the recruitment process.
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister’s Education Adviser Mahdi Amin, Parliamentary Whips Mia Nuruddin Ahmed Apu and Rakibul Islam Bakul, Secondary and Higher Education Division Secretary Abdul Khaleque, Primary and Mass Education Secretary Jesmin Nahar, and other relevant officials attended the meeting.

item.title: Diesel price hike raises irrigation costs for Jamalpur farmers
item.description:
The recent diesel price hike has increased irrigation costs for Aman farmers in Jamalpur, putting additional financial pressure on them during the crucial crop-growing period.
With relatively little rainfall this season, farmers cultivating Aman on higher land have had to rely on regular irrigation. However, the sudden rise in diesel prices has made irrigation more expensive, forcing some farmers to reduce the amount of water they apply to their fields.
In some areas, the lack of adequate irrigation has caused the soil in Aman fields to crack. Farmers fear that delays in irrigation could hamper crop growth and reduce yields.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), around 120,550 hectares of land across Jamalpur’s six upazilas are under Aman cultivation this season. Vegetables and other crops are being cultivated on another 5,000 hectares.
Many farmers in the district depend on diesel-powered irrigation pumps, particularly for higher land. The increase in diesel prices has therefore pushed up their production costs.
Abdul Rahim Mia and Ibrahim Mondal, farmers from Bahadurpur village in Palbandha union of Islampur upazila, said irrigation costs had increased significantly following the diesel price hike. It has become difficult to bear the additional cost at this important stage of Aman cultivation. As a result, they cannot irrigate their fields as needed, they said.
Farmers Kaddus Mia and Abdul Barek of Sirajabad said they were waiting for rain as higher irrigation costs had made it difficult to supply sufficient water to their fields. Insufficient irrigation may disrupt the normal growth of the rice. If yields fall, it will be difficult to recover production costs, they said.
Farmers also said the prices of fertiliser, pesticides, labour and other agricultural inputs had increased. Higher fuel prices have also raised transportation costs for fertiliser and other farm inputs. They fear losses at the end of the season if rice prices do not increase in line with rising production costs.
The farmers have called for measures to make irrigation more affordable and reduce transportation costs of agricultural inputs to ensure uninterrupted Aman cultivation.
DAE Deputy Director Alam Sharif Khan said 120,550 hectares of land had been brought under Aman cultivation in the district this season, while vegetables, including chilli and eggplant, were being grown on around 5,000 hectares.
He said the agriculture department was encouraging farmers to adopt cost-effective and modern irrigation technologies. “Aman farmers are under pressure due to higher irrigation costs. There are concerns that yields may decline if fields do not receive water on time,” he said.
He also added that agriculture officials were regularly visiting fields and providing necessary advice to help farmers achieve their expected yields.

item.title: Dengue claims 8 more lives, 2,036 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Eight more people died of dengue and 2,036 new patients were hospitalised across the country in the 24 hours until 8am on Monday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 233 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the deaths, two died in Dhaka North City Corporation while one each died in Dhaka South City Corporation, Khulna, Chittagong, Barisal, Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 70,750 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 70, 258 have recovered.
